item.title: 12-Year-Old Linux NFS Vulnerability Lets Remote Attackers Gain Root
item.description:
12-Year-Old Linux NFS Vulnerability Lets Remote Attackers Gain Root

A 12‑year‑old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s NFS server, CVE‑2026‑99362, lets remote attackers gain root privileges.

🔍 Overview

  • The flaw, dubbed NFS2ROOT by OpenSec, is a heap buffer overflow in the nfsd server.
  • Remote attackers can send crafted requests that write beyond an allocated buffer.
  • Successful exploitation corrupts kernel memory and grants root access on exposed Linux servers.

🧩 How it Works

  • An attacker sends malicious NFSv4.1 requests causing the server to write past a buffer.
  • This allows reading of kernel memory, bypassing KASLR.
  • A callback is placed in a released memory area that executes a command.
  • When the connection closes, the kernel runs the embedded command with root privileges.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Vulnerability exists since Linux kernel 3.16 (March 2014).
  • Affects kernels older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, or 7.4‑rc1 when nfsd (v4.1 or 4.2) is loaded and TCP port 2049 is reachable over the Internet.
  • No user interaction required; low‑complexity attack.

🚀 Availability

  • ANSSI’s Jérémy Jean submitted a fix in August; the patch was shared with NFSD maintainers in late September.

💡 Why it Matters

  • No wild exploitation reports yet, but the flaw can give attackers full control.
  • Apply the latest kernel security updates immediately and reboot.
  • If patching isn’t possible, restrict TCP port 2049 to trusted clients or disable nfs-server in /etc/nfs.conf.
  • Kernel hardening does not remove the overflow; patch every host.
  • Monitor for signs such as kernel warnings from nfsd4_check_resp_size, shells spawned by kernel workers, bursts of short NFSv4.1 sessions, and kernel oopses with nfsd4_* or svc_* frames.

📚 Related Flaws

  • Other privilege escalation bugs disclosed this year include RefluXFS, CIFSwitch, Dirty Frag, Fragnesia, PinTheft, Copy Fail, Pack2TheRoot, and DirtyDecrypt/DirtyCBC.

#Linux #NFS #KernelSecurity #CVE202699362 #PrivilegeEscalation #CyberSecurity

Source: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges

item.title: Microsoft removes WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028
item.description:
Microsoft removes WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028

Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system, as it encourages enterprises to transition to cloud-based update management tools.

🧩 How it works

WSUS (Windows Server Update Services), introduced in 2005 as Software Update Services (SUS), allows IT administrators to manage and distribute updates for Microsoft products across corporate networks with many Windows devices. It provides centralized control over updates, eliminating the need for each device to download them individually from Microsoft’s servers. While Windows Server 2028 removes this role, WSUS remains available and supported in earlier releases, including Windows Server 2025, for the duration of their support lifecycles. Organizations can continue to use WSUS on those releases to manage updates for supported Windows client and Windows Server releases, which includes updates to Windows Server 2028.

⚙️ Key details

  • Deprecation Status: Microsoft officially deprecated WSUS in September 2024 but stated it plans to maintain functionality and continue publishing updates through the channel. The company noted that WSUS remains operational but is no longer investing in new features.
  • Enterprise Impact: The change affects enterprise environments that rely on WSUS to manage updates but does not impact home users or those using Microsoft Configuration Manager.
  • Security Removals: Windows Server 2028 also removes VBScript (disabled by default in Internet Explorer 11 on Windows 10) and the legacy Windows Management Instrumentation Command-line (WMIC) utility. These removals are intended to thwart a wide range of malware and attack tactics that abuse them. Additionally, Windows Internet Name Service (WINS) support, which was deprecated with the release of Windows Server 2022 in August 2021, is being removed in this version.
  • Recommended Alternatives: Businesses are encouraged to adopt cloud-based solutions for keeping endpoints and servers up to date. In a September 2024 statement, Microsoft’s Nir Froimovici recommended that organizations transition to cloud tools, including Windows Autopatch and Microsoft Intune for client update management, and Azure Update Manager for server update management.

🏭 Enterprise Scenarios

Microsoft recognizes the need to manage updates in disconnected and highly controlled environments. The company stated that it is invested in supporting these scenarios and will share more information as the work progresses.

🚀 Availability

Microsoft announced Windows Server 2028 at the Ignite 2026 conference. Early access is available by registering for the Windows Insider Program for Windows Server or applying to enroll in the Windows Server Technology Adoption Program (TAP).

#Microsoft #WindowsServer #WSUS #ITSecurity #EnterpriseIT

Source: Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028

item.title: Attackers Chain Exploits to Target Exposed Palo Alto Networks Devices
item.description:
Attackers Chain Exploits to Target Exposed Palo Alto Networks Devices

Threat actors are chaining exploits for the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities to target Palo Alto Networks devices with management interfaces exposed to the internet.

🧩 How it works

The attacks combine two distinct security issues:

  • PHP2Shell: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. These allow unauthenticated attackers to run code remotely with the privileges of the PHP web worker.
  • Fragnesia: A Linux kernel vulnerability in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem (CVE-2026-46300) that lets a local attacker with low privileges escalate permissions to root level.

A November 28 alert from CISA warned that these issues were being chained to deploy PHP webshells on vulnerable systems and execute commands as root. Dream Security researchers reported observing a campaign using this specific chain, targeting servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, including a U.S. government affiliate.

⚙️ Key details

  • Exploitation vector: Palo Alto Networks confirmed in an advisory that attacks target firewalls running PAN-OS with their management interface exposed to the public internet.
  • Exposure: The company stated that all observed exploitation activity involved devices that exposed their management interface to the public internet, contrary to recommended best practices.
  • Chaining specifics: While technical details of the chaining were not provided, Palo Alto Networks noted that the observed method is the only known way to exploit the Fragnesia flaw.

🛡️ Mitigation

  • PHP2Shell update: Administrators who already applied updates addressing the PHP2Shell flaw are considered safe from these specific chained attacks.
  • Fragnesia fixes: Fixes have been released for PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2, with the exact patch-carrying build varying by release.
  • Network configuration: For those requiring a remote management interface, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to trusted internal IP addresses.

#Cybersecurity #PaloAltoNetworks #CVE #ZeroDay #SecurityVulnerability

Source: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks

item.title: Threat actors compromised 24 Check Point servers across 22 organizations in cyberespionage campaign
item.description:
Threat actors compromised 24 Check Point servers across 22 organizations in cyberespionage campaign

Threat actors exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise two dozen Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign targeting 22 organizations, according to threat intelligence firm GreyNoise. The activity, tracked as GT13, was confirmed as ongoing between October 17 and November 2, though researchers believe the campaign remains active given the threat actors’ persistent access to Check Point devices. The 22 victim organizations are spread across 17 countries and include government entities, financial services providers, and companies in the energy, transportation, mining, and manufacturing sectors.

🔍 Overview

The attackers launched their operations from 99 IP addresses that appear to come from compromised Check Point devices and ExpressVPN exit nodes. GreyNoise detected the activity and noted it resembled cyberespionage operations, although the attacker’s motivation could not be conclusively determined. The researchers assessed that GT13 operated an AI-powered offensive tool, based on observed behavior, automation, and custom tooling, but this use of AI in the campaign remains unconfirmed.

🧩 How it works

The attack chain began with unknown means of initial compromise, though GreyNoise could not determine when or how the Check Point servers were breached. During post-compromise stages, the researchers observed the exploitation of CVE-2026-16232, an authentication bypass in Check Point SmartConsole that allows attackers to obtain an application login token and authenticate with administrator privileges. A Rejetto HTTP File Server, compromised by exploiting CVE-2026-61500, was used as an operational relay for managing intrusions and collecting stolen data from the compromised environments.

⚙️ Key details

The attackers leveraged automation and custom tooling, observed across more than 1,400 network sessions, 800 command-line artifacts, and 1,200 file-related activities. Their activities included:

  • Stealing firewall databases, credentials, configuration data, and internal certificate authority files
  • Generating a new certificate in one victim’s environment
  • Unloading security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections
  • Conducting internal network reconnaissance and attempting lateral movement

On October 26, the attacker performed a bulk certificate management operation across all 24 compromised Check Point servers, which failed, but still helped GreyNoise identify victims. The researchers also observed attempts to exploit multiple additional vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF), and CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script).

The campaign targeted additional enterprise systems including:

System Vulnerability Notes
Citrix NetScaler CVE-2023-4966 Targeted in lateral movement
Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2024-21893 Targeted during campaign
VMware vCenter CVE-2021-21972, CVE-2023-34048 Multiple vulnerabilities exploited
Microsoft Exchange CVE-2021-26855/34473 Targeted during intrusions
Microsoft Netlogon CVE-2020-1472 Part of lateral movement attempts

BleepingComputer has contacted Check Point to ask if they have better visibility into those attacks and which flaw was exploited for initial access, and we are waiting for their response.

💡 Why it matters

Although GreyNoise lost visibility into the campaign operations on November 2, the researchers believe it could still be ongoing. The company has notified international government partners and CERTs to alert impacted organizations and shared indicators of compromise (IoCs) that could help identify additional intrusions or block future attempts. Check Point warned about CVE-2026-16232 in July, marking it as an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability.

The campaign demonstrates sophisticated attack capabilities using compromised infrastructure and automation tools to conduct large-scale credential theft and lateral movement across critical infrastructure sectors including government, finance, and energy.

#cybersecurity #CheckPoint #GreyNoise #GT13 #cyberespionage #AI

Source: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations

item.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of Critical Cisco Expressway Vulnerability
item.description:
CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of Critical Cisco Expressway Vulnerability

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has warned federal agencies that attackers are actively exploiting a recently patched critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway devices. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-76466, enables unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected devices. Russian cybersecurity company F6 reported that attackers used an unnamed AI assistant to exploit this vulnerability, gaining root access on internet-exposed Cisco Expressway devices and moving laterally across internal network clusters. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and mandated federal agencies to patch within three days under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, while urging all network defenders to prioritize remediation.

#cisa #cisco #vulnerability #cybersecurity #ai-security

Source: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks

item.title: CrowdSec provides open-source IDS/IPS and WAF with community blocklists
item.description:
CrowdSec provides open-source IDS/IPS and WAF with community blocklists

CrowdSec is an open-source, participative security solution that offers crowdsourced server detection and protection against malicious IPs. It operates as an all-in-one IDS/IPS and WAF for Linux, Windows, Docker, and Kubernetes environments, allowing users to detect bad behaviors and actively remediate threats through a shared community blocklist.

🔍 Overview

  • CrowdSec is an open-source security solution that is participative by design.
  • It provides IDS/IPS (Intrusion Detection/Prevention System) and WAF (Web Application Firewall) capabilities.
  • It supports Linux, Windows, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • It features a crowdsourced blocklist of malicious IPs.
  • Detection rules are available under the MIT license.

🧩 How it works

  • Log Analysis: The Security Engine detects bad behaviors by analyzing log sources and HTTP requests.
  • Decoupled Architecture: Following a “Detect Here, Remedy There” approach, users can parse logs on one machine and block threats at a firewall, reverse proxy, or CDN on another.
  • WAF Capabilities: The AppSec component is built on Coraza, allowing SecLang rules and the OWASP Core Rule Set to load as-is. It also supports a YAML rule format.
  • Bot Mitigation: AppSec can answer suspicious requests with a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge at tunable difficulty, stopping headless browsers and scrapers while allowing verified crawlers like Googlebot to pass.
  • Community Blocklist: An IP identified as malicious by one user is added to a curated list, proactively blocking that IP for all other users before it reaches their systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • Scenarios: Ships by default with scenarios for brute force, port scan, and web scan.
  • Customization: Users can extend protection by picking more scenarios from the Hub or creating their own.
  • Remediation: Allows active remediation using Remediation Components.
  • Comparison: Unlike fail2ban, CrowdSec decouples detection and remediation; unlike ModSecurity or naxsi, it shares IP reputation and remediation layers with the log-based engine.

🚀 Availability

  • Installation is available for Linux, Windows, Docker, OpnSense, and Kubernetes.
  • The Community Blocklist is available in real-time.
  • Detection rules are hosted on the CrowdSec Hub.

#CrowdSec #Cybersecurity #IDS #WAF #OpenSource #BotDetection

Source: crowdsecurity/crowdsec

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Vulnerability Leads to Malware on Routers and KVM Devices
item.description:
GL.iNet Cloud Vulnerability Leads to Malware on Routers and KVM Devices

GL.iNet confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote‑management services to install custom malware on customers’ routers and KVM devices, giving attackers backdoor and reverse‑shell access.

🔍 Overview

  • GL.iNet manufactures home and travel routers and KVM devices that allow remote computer control.
  • Its GoodCloud platform lets customers manage supported devices remotely.

🛠️ Exploit Details

  • An unauthorized party exploited a cloud remote‑management vulnerability to access devices and install malicious software (security advisory, Nov 20).
  • Infected devices showed backdoors and root‑level reverse shells that connected to IP 170.39.226.219 using the Linux nc utility.
  • Initial compromise indicator reported by GL.iNet: a process running as crond -i /tmp/.log.

📊 Impact

  • Some users reported backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access.
  • RemoteToHome Consulting examined 183 routers, finding suspicious activity on 152 (24 with root‑level reverse shells, 47 with an older persistent backdoor, 81 with evidence of attacker‑supplied command execution).
  • GL.iNet has not disclosed the total number of impacted customers or whether data was stolen.

⚙️ Response

  • The cloud vulnerability has been fixed and the attack path blocked; new infections via this route are no longer possible.
  • Existing malware remains on compromised devices.
  • Stable firmware updates with additional security fixes are scheduled for release on November 22, 2026.
  • Recommended firmware versions:
Device Minimum Secure Firmware
RM10, RM1, RM1V2, RM1PE, RM4PE 1.10.3
RM10RC 1.10.3 beta
RMQ1 1.8.7

🛡️ Detection & Cleanup

  • GL.iNet linked to a community‑developed scanner that checks for known malware files, suspicious processes, modified utilities, and altered configuration files.
  • The scanner can collect forensic evidence and optionally remove known malware components, but it cannot detect every infection.
  • Developers warn that malicious files stored in configuration directories may survive a regular firmware upgrade; a full firmware reinstall without retaining settings may be required.
  • Users are asked to upload an anonymous report after scanning to help quantify impacted devices.

📌 Recommendations

  • Install the latest security firmware for your specific model as soon as it becomes available.
  • Run the scanner, preserve evidence before resetting devices, avoid restoring potentially infected configurations, and rotate any exposed credentials or access keys.
  • For KVM users, also analyze computers controlled by the KVM for compromise.
  • Consider a clean firmware reinstall if infection cannot be verified as removed.

#GLiNet #Security #Malware #Firmware

Source: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices

item.title: OpenNHP toolkit hides infrastructure using zero-trust cryptography
item.description:
OpenNHP toolkit hides infrastructure using zero-trust cryptography

OpenNHP is a lightweight, cryptography-powered, open-source toolkit implementing Zero Trust security for infrastructure, applications, and data. It serves as the reference implementation of the Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) Network-infrastructure Hiding Protocol (NHP) specification.

🔍 Overview

OpenNHP is designed to hide servers, ports, and domains from the public internet. In the AI era, visibility equates to vulnerability; OpenNHP inverts this model by remaining invisible until trusted. Consequently, scanners, bots, and AI-driven attackers find nothing to attack because nothing answers until a client proves its identity with a single encrypted packet.

🧩 How it works

The toolkit features two core protocols and a modular design inspired by the NIST Zero Trust Architecture:

  • Network-infrastructure Hiding Protocol (NHP): Conceals server ports, IP addresses, and domain names to protect applications and infrastructure from unauthorized access.
  • Data-content Hiding Protocol (DHP): Ensures data security and privacy via encryption and confidential computing, making data “usable but not visible.”

The architecture includes specific components that slot alongside existing IAM, DNS, FIDO, and Zero Trust policy engines:

Component Function
NHP-Agent Client that sends encrypted knock requests to gain access
NHP-Server Authenticates and authorizes requests; runs separately and is architecturally decoupled from the protected host
NHP-AC Access controller that manages firewall rules on the protected server
NHP-Relay HTTP-to-UDP bridge enabling browser-based agents to send NHP knocks via HTTPS
NHP-KGC Key Generation Center for Identity-Based Cryptography (IBC)

The workflow operates on a default-deny gate for every port, IP, and hostname:

  1. Registration (once per device): The agent generates its own key pair and enrolls the public key. The agent requests a one-time password (NHP_OTP), which the Server’s auth plugin delivers to the user (e.g., by email). The agent sends the OTP and its public key (NHP_REG), and the Server binds the key to the user and replies (NHP_RAK). The private key never leaves the device.
  2. Knock (every access): The agent sends an encrypted knock (NHP_KNK) to the Server. The Server validates the knock and sends an operation.

💡 Why it matters

Attackers can’t exploit what they can’t discover. NHP represents a next step in “hide the service first” designs, extending security stacks rather than forking them.

#OpenNHP #ZeroTrust #Cybersecurity #InfrastructureSecurity #OpenSource

Source: OpenNHP/opennhp

item.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence details AI agent hack on universities
item.description:
Amazon Threat Intelligence details AI agent hack on universities

Amazon Threat Intelligence shared findings from an investigation into a Chinese-nexus threat actor who used autonomous AI agents to conduct hacking operations with minimal human involvement. The investigation revealed a campaign targeting IP addresses associated with universities in East Asia outside mainland China over a 48-hour period beginning September 8, 2026.

🔍 Overview

On September 10, 2026, Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn, an open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework, running without authentication. Because the operator left the server publicly accessible, the operational history of the platform was visible to anyone on the internet. This visibility included project configurations, actor prompts, and AI output. The operator wrote prompts in Simplified Chinese, and the timestamps in executed scripts were configured to China Standard Time.

🧩 How it works

Cairn is built as a research and problem-solving engine for defenders. Operating it is simple: given a starting point and an objective in plain language, it coordinates multiple AI agents to find a path to that goal. The actor in this campaign gave the agents a simple goal: “obtain shell access.” Based on a list of targeted IP addresses and that goal, the AI agents planned, executed, and adjusted their approach as they learned, without the operator choosing each next step.

⚙️ Key details

The campaign included several operations that varied widely in complexity and outcome. During the campaign, the agents found a zero-day in an open-source application and used it to gain full control of a server.

Operation Target Duration Key Actions
Redis instance at one university ~16 hours 148 sequential actions; abused replication feature, escaped scripting sandbox, wrote to config files, corrupted memory, attempted Log4Shell injection
University GPU server > 6 hours Researched public presence to build list of ~80 usernames; tested > 30,000 credential combinations against SSH, admin dashboard, network storage, VPN, and campus portal
Open-source medical imaging AI application Not specified Identified framework, mapped API endpoints, found upload endpoint with a filename parameter

In the Redis operation, when initial attempts to take control failed, the agents mapped the internal Docker network topology through a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in a co-located Qdrant instance and launched credential sprays against PostgreSQL, SSH, and several other services. None of these attempts succeeded. In the GPU server operation, the agents never found a working login. Against the medical imaging application, the agents successfully identified the framework and mapped its API endpoints.

💡 Why it matters

These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening. Defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable, as the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction, even when specific operations did not succeed.

#Cybersecurity #AIAgents #ThreatIntelligence #Amazon #Zero-day #AutonomousHacking

Source: Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Broadcom Patches VMware vCenter Zero-Day Exploited by Chinese Group
item.description:
Broadcom Patches VMware vCenter Zero-Day Exploited by Chinese Group

Broadcom has released emergency security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026.

🧩 How it works

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server, a management platform used to manage VMware virtualized environments. According to Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a vulnerable vCenter Server to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.

  • Successful exploitation allows attackers to obtain administrative access to vCenter, giving them control over the virtual machines managed by the server.
  • The vulnerability affects vCenter regardless of whether Enhanced Linked Mode is enabled.

Mandiant researchers documented that attackers exploit the flaw to create a remote authentication bypass, establishing an authenticated session as administrator@vsphere.local. Using this session, attackers can execute arbitrary commands and acquire files, including the data.mdb database, by leveraging the vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC interface vmdirdbcp.

⚙️ Key details

  • Patch Availability: Broadcom patched the vulnerability on November 19 in VMSA-2026-0009. This update also fixes four other vulnerabilities affecting VMware SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows.
  • Affected Software: The advisory notes that users are affected if running any version of VMware vCenter, SDDC Manager, or VMware Tools for Windows prior to the versions listed as “fixed” in the VMSA. This includes vCenter and SDDC Manager deployed standalone and as part of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Telco Cloud Platform, and VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure, as well as VMware Tools installed in Windows virtual machines.
  • Workarounds: Broadcom states there are no official workarounds for the vulnerabilities, although network restrictions and firewall controls can help reduce exposure.
  • Urgency: The company considers the vCenter vulnerability an emergency update, urging organizations to install patches as soon as possible.
Tool/Malware Function
SLIMSAVAGE Web shells deployed to maintain persistent access and scan for VMware systems
BONESAW Custom Golang exploitation tool used to exploit CVE-2026-123890 and steal the directory database
SAWSNAKE Enables “Golden SAML” attacks to forge authentication tokens and bypass MFA
CAGEMATCH Web shell/backdoor used to execute commands and transfer files
BEARBONES Web shell/backdoor used to execute commands and steal credentials
LAZYBONES Web shell/backdoor used to execute commands and maintain access

🚨 Attack Context

Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group revealed that a suspected Chinese state-sponsored hacking group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-123890 in early September 2026. The VMware exploitation was part of the same intrusion campaign, where attackers first compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances (exploiting zero-day CVE-2026-102764) before moving laterally into internal Linux systems.

After gaining access to an internal Linux appliance, the hackers deployed SLIMSAVAGE web shells, escalated privileges to root, and scanned the internal network. They then used BONESAW to compromise a VMware vCenter Server. BONESAW creates a vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO) administrator account and steals the server’s directory database. It can also extract SAML signing keys, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens. Following exploitation, attackers deployed SAWSNAKE and additional backdoors to move deeper into virtualized environments, access ESXi hosts, and extract sensitive information, including Windows Active Directory database files.

💡 Why it matters

Mandiant says the use of two zero-day vulnerabilities in the same campaign, along with multiple malware families tailored to the targeted platforms, demonstrates the threat actor’s technical expertise. Researchers urge admins to apply the VMware security updates as soon as possible and configure additional security controls to protect their virtualization infrastructure.

#VMware #Broadcom #CVE-2026-123890 #ArmoryCastle #ZeroDay #InfoSec

Source: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September

item.title: F5 Warns Customers to Patch Critical BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
item.description:
F5 Warns Customers to Patch Critical BIG-IP Vulnerabilities

US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution.

🔍 Overview

  • Status: NEW
  • Five stack-based buffer overflow flaws affect the BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) and BIG-IP iRules programmable scripting feature.
  • Unauthenticated threat actors can exploit these issues to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) and execute arbitrary code remotely on vulnerable configurations.
  • F5 also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability (CVE-2026-126822) caused by an integer underflow weakness.

🧩 How it works

  • Tracked vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, and CVE-2026-123637.
  • Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts during exploitation.
  • This is a data plane issue only with no control plane exposure.

🚀 Availability

  • F5 stated there are no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances and over 14,600 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online.

💡 Why it matters

  • Although F5 has not flagged any of these issues as exploited in attacks, admins should upgrade systems quickly.
  • Cybercrime and nation-state threat groups have often abused F5 vulnerabilities in the wild to breach corporate networks, map internal servers, hijack devices, deploy data-wiping malware, and steal sensitive files.

#Cybersecurity #F5 #Vulnerabilities #Patch

Source: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
